source.title: Is Stochastic Gradient Descent Near Optimal?
source.authors: Yi-Fan Zhu; Hong Jun Jeon; Benjamin Van Roy

record.file_problem: The supplied text appears to contain the full paper, including appendices; no apparent truncation or garbling that prevents extraction.
record.tranche_reason: The paper tests how fitting-network architecture and width affect test error on natural labels generated by random ReLU teacher networks. Its synthetic regression setup and error measure differ from the claim versions’ classification/generalization-gap settings.
record.gate_note: Rows cover the paper's own fitting-network architecture and width comparisons. The optimizer, batch size, and absence of explicit regularization are setup details, not separately tested results. Cited findings from other studies are not rows.
record.test_reason: No result tests V1–V8. Width comparisons do not establish zero training error or examine widening beyond interpolation (V2); depth comparisons contain no convolutional networks or images (V3). Section 4.2.2 uses the cited small-batch generalization finding to choose batch size 64, without comparing batch sizes (V5).
record.authors_conclusion: The record is broadly accurate. The authors conclude that stochastic gradient training with automatic width tuning nearly attains theoretical sample-complexity upper bounds efficiently for randomly drawn single-hidden-layer ReLU teachers. The implementation uses Adam. They report nearly linear sample and data-query scaling, rather than establishing a near-optimal total computational-complexity bound, and leave multiple-hidden-layer teachers for future work.
record.recipe_differences: Synthetic single-hidden-layer ReLU teacher regression with Gaussian inputs and noise; Adam, automatic width selection, validation-based early stopping and learning-rate decay. The claim versions concern other settings such as classification, explicit generalization gaps, or magnitude-aware measures.
record.method_sensitivity: Test error varied with fitting-network depth and width-selection scheme; the paper reports slightly worse average performance for two- and three-hidden-layer fitting networks than for one hidden layer, and width tuning performed best among tested schemes.

fits_no_version.finding: For single-hidden-layer teachers, two- and three-hidden-layer fitting networks have geometric mean test-error ratios of 1.14–1.38 relative to one-hidden-layer fitting networks.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Matching fitting-network depth to teacher depth improves average prediction error in this synthetic regression setting.

fits_no_version.finding: Automatic width tuning outperforms teacher-matching, 4M, and median-selected widths; the 4M scheme also has lower geometric mean error than the teacher-matching scheme.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Overparameterization relative to teacher width and instance-specific width selection improve prediction in this synthetic regression setting.

record.problems: Synthetic regression task; no random-label memorization or training-error results; no image-classification comparison of convolutional and fully connected architectures. The appendix architecture and width comparisons report summary ratios without uncertainty estimates in their tables.
record.rows_left_out: None. Appendix C Table 3 and Table 5 comparisons are included; other sample-complexity and query-complexity results do not measure a versioned generalization-gap claim.

untested.parts: Random-label fitting and natural-label held-out accuracy versus chance under matched architectures and training recipes.
Test-error behavior as fitting-network width increases beyond the width needed for zero training error.
Convolutional versus fully connected image models, local connectivity, learned sparse connections, and convolutional initialization.
Adaptive optimizer versus SGD generalization and dependence on tuning, weight decay, or switching optimizers.
Batch-size comparisons under fixed epoch budgets and adaptations that reduce large-batch penalties.
Dropout interventions, training-set size, underfitting, and interactions with augmentation and weight decay.
Magnitude-aware sharpness ranking generalization gaps against alternative measures.
Retraining after removing highly memorized examples versus equally many random examples.

record.verdict_notes: Teacher width M in the sample-complexity experiments controls the data-generating task; it is not a post-interpolation sweep of fitting-network width. Absence of dropout and weight decay is a setup choice, not evidence about their effects.

versions.untested_parts: Random-label memorization and natural-label test accuracy versus chance.
The stated one-hidden-layer ReLU width sweep on MNIST and downsampled CIFAR-10; zero training error and the interpolation threshold.
Convolutional versus fully connected image classifiers and the role of local connectivity.
Comparisons among adaptive optimizers and SGD, including the effects of tuning, weight decay, or optimizer switching.
Large versus small batches under fixed epoch budgets and recipe adaptations.
Dropout and weight-decay interventions on classification tasks.
Magnitude-aware sharpness and other measures tracking the training-test gap.
Removing memorized examples and measuring the effect on test accuracy.
